sections.title: Major Strategies
sections.sub: The core techniques nearly every solo relies on

entries.name: Catch Tank
entries.desc: Catch tanks intercept and absorb energy from a high-damaging charge move. The energy absorbed is used to return their own quick, high-damage charge move.

entries.name: Tick Perfect Cast
entries.desc: Precisely timing the final tap — not spamming — just before a charge move cast. Successful TPC avoids the energy resolve DPS nerf; very hard to execute consistently.

entries.name: Clean Exit
entries.desc: Relobbying during a charge move's animation for maximum energy efficiency and time savings.

entries.name: Rejoin
entries.desc: A rejoin lasting 6.5–7 seconds, only utilizing potions to quickly re-enter the fight.

entries.name: Execute
entries.desc: Executing a boss with a low animation-duration or low-cost charge move.

entries.name: Hot Swap
entries.desc: Switching to the next available attacker when the current attacker cannot reach another charge move.

entries.name: Recycle
entries.desc: Reusing the same Main DPS Pokémon across multiple rejoins instead of a fresh one each time.

sections.title: Advanced / Minor Strategies
sections.sub: Refinements layered on top of the core techniques

entries.name: Hotswap Chain
entries.desc: When a boss casts charge moves in rapid succession, forcing the user to Catch Tank from one attacker straight into the next in rapid succession. Heavily RNG-based, but the highest DPS cycle achievable in a raid.

entries.name: Combo Charge Move
entries.desc: Using a small charge move when the enemy charge move would otherwise overflow in energy. e.g. Necrozma Dusk Mane lowering energy with an Iron Head before tanking a full Earthquake if Sunsteel Strike can't be cast in time.

entries.name: Charge Move Buffer
entries.desc: When swapping — mainly to perform a Catch Tank — you can immediately cast a charge move (if you have the energy for it) without a fast move first, by buffering a charged move from your active Pokémon.

entries.name: Trailing Catch Tank
entries.desc: A 6th Pokémon used to catch trailing charge moves when nearing a rejoin. This trailing Pokémon typically uses low energy-cost moves (Breaking Swipe, Aura Sphere, etc.) to increase consistency.

entries.name: Advanced Rejoin
entries.desc: A rejoin lasting 5.5 seconds. Upon exiting the raid, the user first swipes to their party and buffers the animation by tapping the heal bag. This interaction saves roughly 1.0 second on average.

entries.name: Charge Move Delay
entries.desc: Used against bosses with 1-bar charge moves. Intentionally delaying 2-bar or 3-bar charge move casts to force out fast moves instead — usually giving the player 2 free fast moves.

entries.name: Double Catch Tank
entries.desc: A Catch Tank intercepts two charge moves on separate ocassions. During the second swap the sum of the energy gained, paired with fast moves, is used to quickly fire back a heavy hitting charge move.

entries.name: Substitute
entries.desc: Primary DPSer moves to the 2nd slot from the 2nd cycle onwards to avoid rejoining into a lethal charge move. A substitute (usually a Catch Tank) is moved to the first slot.

sections.title: Expensive “Whaling” Strategies
sections.sub: High-investment techniques for pushing the hardest content

entries.name: Double Battle Party
entries.desc: Using two identical battle parties; reduces every other rejoin time by about 40%. It can also create ideal Recommended Rejoins, which is a one-time time save.
